simulator.ion_shield_ranged_only.quoted_text: This model has a 5+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks only.
simulator.ion_shield_ranged_only.trigger: A melee attack is resolved against an Imperial Knights model whose profile has invuln_ranged_only=True (set via data/overrides.json on the standard-codex Questoris/Dominus Knights and Armigers, which carry the shared BSData 5+* Ion Shield profile 'Imperium - Imperial Knights - Library.cat.gz' targetId 8552-862d-6a49-4879).
simulator.ion_shield_ranged_only.effect: The datasheet invulnerable save is suppressed (set to none) for melee attacks, so a big Imperial Knight defends melee with only its 3+ armour save. Against ranged attacks the 5+ invulnerable still applies. Implemented in code/units.py save resolution (mode == 'melee' and target.profile.invuln_ranged_only). Chaos Knights' Ion Shield is ranged AND melee per the Chaos Knights codex, so invuln_ranged_only is left False for them; Forge World Acastus / Questoris Magaera-Styrix variants are not flagged (their Ion Aegis shields are unverified and none are fielded in the archetype lists).

simulator.code_chivalric.rule_name: Code Chivalric (Oath of Honour — martial-valour Quality)
simulator.code_chivalric.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is IMPERIAL KNIGHTS, at the end of the Read Mission Objectives step, you must determine your army's Oath for the coming battle. An Oath consists of two parts - one Deed and one Quality. [Quality: ...with our martial valour risen over all.] Each time this model is selected to shoot or fight, you can re-roll one Hit roll and you can re-roll one Wound roll.
simulator.code_chivalric.trigger: Attacker's army faction is Imperial Knights and the army has taken the 'martial valour' Quality at battle start (SwegHammer always picks this Quality — the other two Qualities are a Move/Advance/Charge bump and an OC/Leadership bump that the simulator cannot express).
simulator.code_chivalric.effect: Re-roll ONE Hit roll and ONE Wound roll per activation — a single re-roll of each, spent on the first failed die. Because SwegHammer instantiates one Unit per model, the codex's 'Each time this model is selected to shoot or fight' maps exactly onto one re-roll per Unit activation, so this is now a faithful implementation rather than an approximation. (Wave 71 fidelity fix: the previous implementation re-rolled EVERY natural 1, which over-scaled with shot volume — a 20-shot Knight gun got ~3-4 effective re-rolls instead of the rule's one, inflating Imperial Knights damage on the high-volume platforms.) The implementation lives in code/units.py:Unit.attack via the per-activation _chiv_hit_reroll / _chiv_wound_reroll budget, faction-gated to 'Imperial Knights' so the Chaos Knights army rule (Harbingers of Dread, a battle-shock aura that requires per-unit battleshock state the sim does not yet track) is untouched.

VALOURSTRIKE_LANCE.bold_gallantry.quoted_text: Each time an ^^Imperial Knights^^ unit from your army Advances, until the end of the turn, ranged weapons equipped by ^^Imperial Knights^^ models from your army have the [ASSAULT] ability.
VALOURSTRIKE_LANCE.bold_gallantry.trigger: Any Imperial Knights unit Advances (attacker.uid in Battle._advanced_this_round) AND the army's detachment carries bold_gallantry=True AND attacker.profile.faction == 'Imperial Knights'.
VALOURSTRIKE_LANCE.bold_gallantry.effect: The Advance-lockout in Battle._do_shoot is skipped for the advancing IK unit, mirroring the [ASSAULT] keyword grant on all IK ranged weapons. Army-wide: any IK unit that Advances individually benefits (each is independently in _advanced_this_round).

VALOURSTRIKE_LANCE.bondsman_enabled.rule_name: Bondsman abilities (Valourstrike Lance detachment — Paladin's Duty proxy)
VALOURSTRIKE_LANCE.bondsman_enabled.quoted_text: In your Command phase, one or more models from your army with a Bondsman ability can use that ability. For each one that does, select one friendly ^^Armiger^^ model within 12" of that model (you cannot select an ^^Armiger^^ model that is already being affected by a Bondsman ability). Until the start of your next Command phase, that ^^Armiger^^ model is affected by that Bondsman ability. [Paladin's Duty (Bondsman): While a model is affected by this ability, weapons equipped by that model have the [LETHAL HITS] ability, and melee weapons equipped by that model have the [LANCE] ability.]
VALOURSTRIKE_LANCE.bondsman_enabled.trigger: Start of each Command phase, for each alive TITANIC+CHARACTER Imperial Knights unit ('giver'), the first alive non-TITANIC IK unit ('Armiger receiver') anywhere in the army receives the Paladin's Duty buff. GIVER SCOPE (SWEG_IK_BONDSMAN_SCOPED, default-on): Knight Castellan, Knight Valiant, and Canis Rex are TITANIC+CHARACTER but carry NO Bondsman ability on their datasheets (BSData 'Imperium - Imperial Knights' cat — the Dominus-class Castellan/Valiant and the Freeblade Canis Rex have their own abilities), so they are EXCLUDED as givers; every other TITANIC+CHARACTER Knight (the Questoris and Cerastus variants) does carry Bondsman and remains a giver. =0 restores the over-broad keyword-only gate. The codex '12" range' gate is dropped (APPROXIMATION) because SwegHammer's grid-free deployment spreads Armigers further apart than real tables allow — in real games Armigers always deploy within 12" of their bonded lord. Each Armiger can only be buffed once per round.
VALOURSTRIKE_LANCE.bondsman_enabled.effect: (APPROXIMATION) Paladin's Duty is applied as a proxy for all Questoris/Cerastus class Bondsman abilities. Real rule has 6+ distinct Bondsman variants per knight sub-type (Paladin, Warden, Crusader, Gallant, Errant, Preceptor). SwegHammer applies Paladin's Duty (transient_lethal_hits + transient_lance_this_turn) uniformly — the strongest cleanly representable Bondsman buff. Warden's Duty (Sustained Hits 1 + Ignores Cover) and Crusader's Duty (+1 to hit ranged) are deferred.

simulator.damaged_objective_control_brac.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/factions/imperial-knights/ (datasheet 'Damaged' ability); verbatim text below extracted from the canonical BSData cache 'Imperium - Imperial Knights.cat.gz' / 'Chaos - Chaos Knights.cat.gz' (codex-tagged, Knight T11/W26) on 2026-06-01
simulator.damaged_objective_control_brac.rule_name: Damaged: Wounds Remaining — Objective Control reduction (Imperial / Chaos Knights datasheets)
simulator.damaged_objective_control_brac.quoted_text: While this model has 1-9 wounds remaining, subtract 5 from this model's Objective Control characteristic and each time this model makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll. [Armiger / War Dog variant: While this model has 1-5 wounds remaining, subtract 3 from this model's Objective Control characteristic ...; Dominus-class variant: While this model has 1-10 wounds remaining, subtract 5 ...]
simulator.damaged_objective_control_brac.trigger: An Imperial Knights or Chaos Knights model is on its Damaged bracket (current wounds <= the chassis threshold: Armiger/War Dog 5, Questoris 9, Dominus 10) when its Objective Control is summed for objective scoring (Battle._effective_oc, called from _oc_within and _assign_army_oc).
simulator.damaged_objective_control_brac.effect: The model's Objective Control is reduced by the datasheet amount (Armiger/War Dog −3, Questoris/Dominus −5), floored at 0, so a chipped Knight controls objectives less strongly — opponents that shoot a Knight down can then contest it off a marker. Only the Knight factions carry this datasheet rule, so the faction gate is the faithful per-datasheet implementation. ONLY the Objective-Control half of the Damaged ability is modelled here; the −1-to-Hit half is `simulator.damaged_hit_bracket` (wave 188). NOTE: a Goonhammer codex review suggested the current-codex Questoris value might be −4 (Objective Control 10 → 6); RESOLVED (watchdog Q9) to use the canonical BSData cache value −5 — BSData rule-6 governs, and the −4 came from an unreliable web summary. The ±1 is metric-negligible either way.

simulator.damaged_hit_bracket.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/factions/imperial-knights/Knight-Paladin and /Armiger-Warglaive (datasheet 'Damaged' ability), cross-checked with the canonical BSData cache 'Imperium - Imperial Knights.cat.gz' / 'Chaos - Chaos Knights.cat.gz' (the same 'Damaged' rows that govern simulator.damaged_objective_control_bracket); both Wahapedia datasheets verified verbatim 2026-06-05
simulator.damaged_hit_bracket.rule_name: Damaged: Wounds Remaining — minus 1 to the Hit roll (Imperial / Chaos Knights datasheets)
simulator.damaged_hit_bracket.quoted_text: While this model has 1-9 wounds remaining, subtract 5 from this model's Objective Control characteristic and each time this model makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll. [Armiger / War Dog: While this model has 1-5 wounds remaining, subtract 3 from this model's Objective Control characteristic and each time this model makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll. Dominus-class: 1-10 wounds remaining, subtract 5 ... and subtract 1 from the Hit roll.]
simulator.damaged_hit_bracket.trigger: An Imperial Knights or Chaos Knights model makes an attack (shooting OR melee) while on its Damaged bracket (current wounds <= the chassis threshold: Armiger/War Dog 5, Questoris 9, Dominus 10). Modelled in Unit.attack via hit_mod_delta -= 1, gated SWEG_DMGHIT (default OFF for the isolation A/B), same faction gate + thresholds as Battle._effective_oc.
simulator.damaged_hit_bracket.effect: Each of the damaged Knight's attacks suffers −1 to the Hit roll (3+ becomes 4+), composing with the 10e ±1 Hit-modifier cap. The simulator previously modelled only the Objective-Control half of the Damaged ability (wave 85), so a chipped Knight kept full accuracy and over-killed through the back half of every game — a real contributor to the Imperial Knights over-rate (the over-pole). This is the second, previously-unmodelled half of the same datasheet rule whose verbatim text was already cited under simulator.damaged_objective_control_bracket. Applies to BOTH shooting and melee ('makes an attack'). Even-handed within the rule (it is the Knight's own datasheet penalty, not a per-opponent fudge).

simulator.damaged_bracket.notes: 10e datasheet 'Damaged: 1-X Wounds Remaining' ability — a near-universal big-model rule (the wave-190b BSData audit found the offensive Hit penalty on 94 datasheets across 25 of 31 faction files). Per-unit thresholds + penalties are extracted from the canonical BSData cache (data/bsdata/cache/*.cat.gz, rule 7) by code.bsdata.mapper.extract_damaged_bracket. Representative datasheets verified verbatim 2026-06-05: T'au Stormsurge (https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/factions/t-au-empire/) and Imperial Knight Paladin / Armiger Warglaive (https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/factions/imperial-knights/).
simulator.damaged_bracket.rule_name: Damaged: Wounds Remaining (generalized — every model with a real datasheet bracket)
simulator.damaged_bracket.quoted_text: While this model has 1-5 wounds remaining, subtract 3 from this model's Objective Control characteristic, and each time this model makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll. [T'au Stormsurge, verbatim.] Hit-only example (Aeldari Wraithknight): While this model has 1-6 wounds remaining, each time this model makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll.
simulator.damaged_bracket.trigger: ANY model with a real 10e Damaged: 1-X Wounds Remaining datasheet bracket makes an attack (shooting OR melee) while at 1..X current wounds. The per-unit threshold X and the Objective-Control / Hit-roll penalties are read from UnitProfile.damaged_threshold / damaged_oc_penalty / damaged_hit_penalty (mapper-extracted from BSData), gated SWEG_DMGBRACKET. Supersedes the Knight-only simulator.damaged_objective_control_bracket / simulator.damaged_hit_bracket heuristic when set (elif — no double-application).
simulator.damaged_bracket.effect: While damaged, the model Objective Control is reduced by its datasheet damaged_oc_penalty (Battle._effective_oc) and each of its attacks suffers minus damaged_hit_penalty to the Hit roll (Unit.attack). Data-driven and even-handed: it models the SAME real rule for every datasheet that has it, removing the metric-favorable bias of the Knight-only implementation (the sim previously degraded only the 6 Knight datasheets while ~88 other big models — Custodes dreadnoughts, Tau Stormsurge/Riptide, World Eaters, AdMech, Necrons — kept full accuracy + Objective Control while damaged). v1 models the Objective-Control and Hit-roll effects; Attacks-degradation does not occur in any 10e bracket (verified, count 0) and Move-degradation is deferred (not modelled).

simulator.ik_rotate_ion_shields.rule_name: Rotate Ion Shields (Imperial Knights Household stratagem)
simulator.ik_rotate_ion_shields.quoted_text: ROTATE ION SHIELDS — 1CP. Wargear Stratagem. WHEN: Your opponent's Shooting phase, just after an enemy unit has selected its targets. TARGET: One IMPERIAL KNIGHTS unit from your army that was selected as the target of one or more of the attacking unit's attacks. EFFECT: Until the end of the phase, models in your unit have a 4+ invulnerable save.
simulator.ik_rotate_ion_shields.trigger: The opponent's Shooting phase, just after an enemy unit has selected a friendly IMPERIAL KNIGHTS unit as the target of one or more of its attacks.
simulator.ik_rotate_ion_shields.effect: The defending army spends 1 Command Point so that, until the end of the phase, every model in the targeted IMPERIAL KNIGHTS unit has a 4+ invulnerable save. Implemented as Battle._maybe_rotate_ion_shields (env-gated SWEG_IK_ROTATE_IONS, default ON), hooked at the target-selection point in Battle._do_shoot immediately after the Go To Ground hook, sharing its mechanism (Battle._maybe_ion_shield_stratagem) with Chaos Knights' Diabolic Bulwark (simulator.ck_diabolic_bulwark), which prints byte-identical text. The 4+ invulnerable save is applied via the existing transient_invuln_4 flag at the save-resolution branch in Unit.attack (only overriding a worse invuln), the same shared slot Glamour of Tzeentch / Daemonic Invulnerability use for their own 'flat 4+ invuln for the round' grants. The printed 'until the end of the phase' duration is collapsed to the round (cleared with the other per-round transient flags in Battle._clear_transient_stratagem_flags) — the same simplification already accepted for Go To Ground — because this army is the defender in exactly one Shooting phase per round under the I-go-U-go turn structure. Restricted to once per phase (the generic 10e core restriction that the same Stratagem cannot be used more than once in the same phase) via the rotate_ion_shields_used_this_phase flag on Army, reset once per round. The Command Point is only spent when the incoming fire genuinely threatens the target, reusing Battle._ranged_expected_wounds (the same expected-incoming-damage helper Go To Ground and Focus Fire already use) at >= 50% of the targeted model's current health, so a stray shot does not burn the Command Point. Gate unset reproduces the baseline byte-for-byte (no Command Point spent, no flag set, no extra random draws).

simulator.ik_canis_single.rule_name: Sir Hekhtur the Chainbreaker (Canis Rex datasheet, 10e) — phantom second Knight removed
simulator.ik_canis_single.quoted_text: Sir Hekhtur cannot be selected as the target of any of your Stratagems other than Core Stratagems. Your Canis Rex unit is not considered to be destroyed until Sir Hekhtur is also destroyed.
simulator.ik_canis_single.trigger: SWEG_IK_CANIS_SINGLE default-on ('0' is the byte-identical kill-switch); catalogue load of imperial_knights_library_canis_rex (code/bsdata/loader.py _apply_override merge)
simulator.ik_canis_single.effect: DATA-CORRECTNESS FIX. BSData folds Sir Hekhtur — the ejected-pilot replacement model, a 3-wound INFANTRY character who per the datasheet only exists after the Canis Rex model is destroyed — into the Canis Rex entry as a second model_loadouts slot, and the mapper emitted min_models=max_models=2. The per-model squad builder (code/army.py _add_squad_per_model) then spawned one Unit per slot with BOTH inheriting the shared profile health of 26, so every simulated Imperial Knights game fielded TWO permanent 26-wound TITANIC combatants under the Canis Rex name from turn 1 (the archetype seed guarantees Canis Rex in 100% of Imperial Knights builds — the deterministic greedy walk anchor). The gate sets min_models=max_models=1 and drops the Sir Hekhtur loadout slot, fielding the real single Knight. APPROXIMATION / honest omission: the post-destruction Sir Hekhtur bail-out (and the 'not destroyed until Hekhtur is destroyed' clause) is unmodelled — a far smaller infidelity than the phantom double Knight it replaces. BSData source: Imperium - Imperial Knights - Library.cat.gz, Sir Hekhtur unit id 5174-754e-83a-30f (quoted text verified verbatim in the cache). Off path (SWEG_IK_CANIS_SINGLE=0) restores the verbatim two-slot entry byte-identically.

simulator.ik_invuln_ranged_only_batch2.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/factions/imperial-knights/Knight-Destrier, .../Acastus-Knight-Asterius, .../Acastus-Knight-Porphyrion, .../Cerastus-Knight-Castigator, .../Knight-Defender; verbatim ability text below extracted directly from the canonical BSData cache 'Imperium - Imperial Knights - Library.cat.gz' (rule 6 governs; durability fidelity wave, audit B, docs/_DURA_AUDIT_B_DEFENSES.md divergence 1)
simulator.ik_invuln_ranged_only_batch2.rule_name: Ion Shield (five additional Imperial Knight chassis, batch 2)
simulator.ik_invuln_ranged_only_batch2.quoted_text: This model has a 5+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks only. [Knight Defender variant, profile id 5a7a-57fa-9801-4e25: This model has a 4+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks only.]
simulator.ik_invuln_ranged_only_batch2.trigger: SWEG_IK_INVULN_RANGED_ONLY_BATCH2 default-on ('0' is the byte-identical kill-switch); catalogue load of imperial_knights_library_knight_destrier, imperial_knights_library_acastus_knight_asterius, imperial_knights_library_acastus_knight_porphyrion, imperial_knights_library_cerastus_knight_castigator, or imperial_knights_library_knight_defender (code/bsdata/loader.py _apply_override merge). All five reuse the identical shared BSData Ion Shield infoLink shape (profile id 8552-862d-6a49-4879 for the 5+ variant, 5a7a-57fa-9801-4e25 for the Knight Defender 4+ variant) already carried, unconditionally, by every Imperial Knight chassis in the file.
simulator.ik_invuln_ranged_only_batch2.effect: DATA-CORRECTNESS FIX. The mapper's Shape 1 path (code/bsdata/mapper.py extract_invuln, _INVULN_RE) reads the digit straight off the infoLink's own name (e.g. 'Invulnerable Save (5+*)') and immediately continues, never resolving the asterisked target profile's Description text — so the ranged-only qualifier was silently dropped for these five chassis and they carried an unconditional invulnerable save into melee combat. The twelve sibling chassis that use the identical infoLink shape (Armiger Helverin/Moirax/Warglaive, Canis Rex, Knight Castellan/Crusader/Errant/Gallant/Paladin/Preceptor/Valiant/Warden) were already hand-corrected via the invuln_ranged_only override key in data/overrides.json; these five were missed. The gate forces invuln_ranged_only=True for these five catalogue keys, which suppresses the invulnerable save for melee attacks (code/units.py save resolution, mode == 'melee' and profile.invuln_ranged_only / the per-attack invuln_save_melee=7 conversion) while leaving the ranged invulnerable save (5+, or 4+ for Knight Defender) intact. Off path (SWEG_IK_INVULN_RANGED_ONLY_BATCH2=0) restores the unconditional (melee == ranged) invulnerable save byte-identically.

simulator.ik_acheron_invuln.source: https://wahapedia.ru/wh40k10ed/factions/imperial-knights/Cerastus-Knight-Acheron; verbatim ability text below extracted directly from the canonical BSData cache 'Imperium - Imperial Knights - Library.cat.gz' (rule 6 governs; durability fidelity wave, audit B, docs/_DURA_AUDIT_B_DEFENSES.md divergence 2)
simulator.ik_acheron_invuln.rule_name: Ion Shield (Imperial Cerastus Knight Acheron — invulnerable save restored)
simulator.ik_acheron_invuln.quoted_text: This model has a 5+ invulnerable save against ranged attacks only.
simulator.ik_acheron_invuln.trigger: SWEG_IK_ACHERON_INVULN default-on ('0' is the byte-identical kill-switch); catalogue load of imperial_knights_library_cerastus_knight_acheron (code/bsdata/loader.py _apply_override merge).
simulator.ik_acheron_invuln.effect: DATA-CORRECTNESS FIX. BSData authors this unit's Ion Shield ability as an inline Abilities profile named after the unit itself ('Cerastus Knight Acheron', typeName Abilities, id 7afa-5443-53e3-5707 — verified as a single occurrence in the cache file, inline on the Acheron's own selectionEntry id 11d3-167b-6dff-a4c2) rather than the conventional 'Invulnerable Save...' name every other chassis in the same file uses, so the mapper's Shape 3 name-prefix filter (code/bsdata/mapper.py extract_invuln, which requires the profile's own name to start with 'invulnerable save') never matches it and the unit carried NO invulnerable save at all (invuln_save_melee=invuln_save_ranged=7 in data/bsdata/parsed.json and the live catalogue, pre-fix). The Chaos-side twin, 'Chaos Cerastus Knight Acheron' (Chaos - Chaos Knights Library.cat.gz), authors the identical ability under the conventional 'Invulnerable Save' name and is already parsed correctly (invuln_save_melee=7, invuln_save_ranged=5). The gate forces invuln_ranged_only=True and invuln_save_ranged=5 (invuln_save=5 for the legacy single-value field) for this one catalogue key, restoring the real 5+ ranged-only invulnerable save without touching any other unit. Fixed at the loader layer (rather than the mapper/parsed.json layer) so the kill-switch can be validated at eval time without a parsed.json regeneration cycle, matching the SWEG_IK_CANIS_SINGLE / SWEG_NECRON_LYCHGUARD_INVULN precedent for this exact class of BSData-shape-blind-spot bug. Off path (SWEG_IK_ACHERON_INVULN=0) restores the no-invulnerable-save-at-all state byte-identically.

simulator.ik_defender_selfless_protector.quoted_text: Each time a ranged attack is allocated to an Imperial Knights model from your army, if that model is not fully visible to every model in the attacking unit because of this Knight Defender model, that model has the Benefit of Cover and a 4+ invulnerable save against that attack.
simulator.ik_defender_selfless_protector.trigger: SWEG_IK_DEFENDER_COVER default-on ('0' is the byte-identical kill-switch); a ranged attack is allocated to an alive Imperial Knights model (other than the Knight Defender itself) in an army that also fields an alive Knight Defender
simulator.ik_defender_selfless_protector.effect: The screened Imperial Knights target gains the Benefit of Cover (+1 to the armour saving throw, via the in_cover flag) AND a 4+ invulnerable save against that attack (only overriding a worse invuln, via the ik_defender_cover_active flag). BSData source: Imperium - Imperial Knights - Library.cat.gz, inline Abilities profile id af51-9630-82a3-172d on the Knight Defender's own selectionEntry (verified verbatim). No radius is printed anywhere in the ability -- it is a line-of-sight screening ability (gated on the Knight Defender's own silhouette actually blocking the attacking unit's view), not a fixed-range aura. APPROXIMATION, same shape as the Combined Arms 'Stalwart Protector' stratagem's CLEAN MAPPING with approximate eligibility: the sim has no per-third-party line-of-sight-obstruction geometry (only attacker-to-target line of sight is modelled), so the true screened-specifically-by-the-Knight-Defender condition is approximated as 'an alive Knight Defender is present anywhere in the defending army' (Battle._ik_defender_screening_active). Implemented in Battle._do_shoot, bracketed per-attack around the single Unit.attack call exactly like the terrain in_cover / in_heavy_cover flags -- NOT a per-round transient, because the real ability has no duration or Command Point cost; it simply re-applies each time a ranged attack is allocated. Read at the cover application (in_cover) and the invulnerable-save resolution branch (only-if-better 4+) in Unit.attack. Off path (SWEG_IK_DEFENDER_COVER=0) leaves ik_defender_cover_active permanently False -- byte-identical.
